summary:
• Problem: In the valleys of Cochabamba, climate change has made rainfall and temperatures unpredictable, while
  steep altitude variations (2,550 to 2,850 m.a.s.l.) cause recurring crop losses from frosts and droughts due to a
  lack of accessible tools for local farmers.
  • Solution: Kallpa Allpa is a bilingual web platform (Spanish/Quechua) combining real-time NASA satellite data,
  SoilGrids soil analysis, and an altitude-calibrated Machine Learning model to advise farmers on what to sow today
  and successfully forecast the next 3 months.
details:
1. Technical Fixes & UI Enhancements

• Quarterly Projection (+1 and +2 months):

Corrected the month offset logic in app/ml/predictor.py:350. When selecting the base sowing month (e.g., September),

subsequent months are now accurately labeled as «+1 month» (October) and «+2 months» (November).

• Spelling, Accents & Grammar:

Fixed all missing Spanish accents and punctuation marks across app/static/index.html in titles, selectors, forms,

and crop detail cards (Planificación, ¿Dónde está tu terreno...?, Precipitación, Elevación, Suelo fértil, Óptimo,

etc.).

• Units & Terminology:

Replaced the colloquial label «Calor promedio» with «Temperatura promedio» (Average Temperature), and specified

rainfall units explicitly as mm/month on both the main dashboard and quarterly cards.

• High-Contrast Header:

Enhanced the «Kallpa Allpa Cochabamba» top header using a deep Andean green and navy gradient (linear-

gradient(135deg, #0f4a24, #073b61)), crisp white typography (#ffffff), and text shadows to ensure high contrast and

readability under any display conditions.

• Institutional Footer Identification:

Designed a formal footer featuring badge cards for the challenge (NASA Space Apps Challenge), the team (Kallpa

Shift), the university (Universidad Simón I. Patiño - USIP), and scientific data sources (NASA POWER & SoilGrids

ISRIC).

• Live Demo Contingency Backup:

Generated a high-resolution, full-page screenshot stored in the local captures directory:

capturas/01_vista_completa_sistema.png (ready for slide decks or fallback during pitch presentations).

2. The Solution (Kallpa Allpa Cochabamba)

• Problem: In the valleys of Cochabamba, climate change has made rainfall and temperatures unpredictable, while

steep altitude variations (2,550 to 2,850 m.a.s.l.) cause constant crop losses due to unseasonal frosts and droughts,

exacerbated by a lack of accessible tools for local farmers.

• Solution: Kallpa Allpa is a bilingual web platform (Spanish/Quechua) combining real-time NASA satellite climate

data, SoilGrids soil properties, and an altitude-calibrated Machine Learning (Random Forest) model, providing

farmers with actionable crop suitability recommendations today and reliable quarterly forecasts.
